s1.syndrome_frame: a chronic skin condition characterized by asymptomatic red to brown macules and papules with a symmetric distribution on the trunk and extremities
salient_findings: red to brown macules and papules on trunk and extremities
nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils in skin biopsy
key_facts: male patient in his 20s
12-month history of skin lesions
lesions initially appeared on trunk and spread to upper and proximal lower extremities
lesions were symmetrically distributed and did not coalesce
face, distal extremities, and mucous membranes were unaffected
some lesions resolved spontaneously with residual hyperpigmentation
hypereosinophilia (4220/μL)
elevated tryptase (33.7 ng/mL)
elevated vitamin B12 (>6000 pg/mL)
negative serologic tests for HIV, hepatitis A, B, and C
negative tests for parasitic infections
skin biopsy showed nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils
bone marrow analysis showed hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia and increased eosinophils

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils in skin biopsy, elevated tryptase, and hypereosinophilia

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with symmetric distribution, nodular infiltration of histiocytes, and elevated vitamin B12

shortlist.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils in skin biopsy, and negative serologic tests for infectious diseases

shortlist.label: Mastocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated tryptase, hypereosinophilia, and skin lesions with symmetric distribution

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypereosinophilia, elevated tryptase, and skin lesions with symmetric distribution

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of skin lesions with nodular infiltration of histiocytes, lymphocytes, and eosinophils, along with elevated tryptase and hypereosinophilia, is more consistent with mastocytosis. The presence of the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene is not typical for mastocytosis but the overall clinical and pathological picture leans more towards mastocytosis.

rejected.label: Chronic eosinophilic leukemia
rejected.why: While the patient has hypereosinophilia and increased eosinophils in the bone marrow, the skin biopsy findings and clinical presentation are more characteristic of mastocytosis. The FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene is more commonly associated with chronic eosinophilic leukemia, but the overall picture is not fully consistent with this diagnosis.
